description: The figure presents a comparative analysis of the performance of various large language models (LLMs) on the MATH-500 and AIME24 benchmarks, illustrating the effectiveness of compute-optimal test-time scaling (TTS) versus chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in smaller models. The left side of the figure (panels a–c) focuses on MATH-500, while the right side (panels d–f) displays results for AIME24. Each panel compares multiple LLMs, with bar heights representing performance scores on the vertical axis, which ranges from 65 to 100 for MATH-500 and 0 to 90 for AIME24. In panel (a), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (78.2) outperforms Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (71.4) and GPT-4o (74.6) on MATH-500. Panel (b) shows that DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B (91.6) surpasses o1-mini (90.0) and o1-preview (85.5). In panel (c), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (97.3) exceeds the performance of Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (95.2) and o1 (94.8). On AIME24, panel (d) reveals that Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (30.0) outperforms Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (23.3) and o1-mini (9.3). Panel (e) shows DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B (63.6) surpassing o1-mini (63.3) and o1-preview (44.6). Finally, panel (f) demonstrates that DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (83.3) outperforms both DeepSeek-R1 (79.8) and o1 (79.2). The results collectively suggest that smaller LLMs employing TTS can achieve superior performance compared to larger models using CoT, particularly on these challenging mathematical reasoning tasks.
